findings.title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is a no-op now that `.small-action` is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` is converted to `display: flex` (line 264), which makes its direct children (`.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, and the action `button`s) flex items. Per the CSS Flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the retained `button { float: right; }` (line 309) and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) no longer do anything. Previously the edit/delete buttons on small-action posts were pushed to the right edge by the float; after this change they will sit immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text (which has no `flex: 1` or `margin-left: auto` counterpart) unless some other stylesheet happens to give the description a fixed width. This is a visual regression in the small-action post layout. The fix is to replace the float with `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) and drop the now-dead float declarations.

findings.title: `order()` mixin passes the standard `order` value straight through to legacy `box-ordinal-group`, whose scale is different
findings.body: The new `order($val)` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val` alongside standard `order: $val`. The 2009 box model's `box-ordinal-group` is a positive integer with a default of 1, whereas standard `order` defaults to 0 and accepts 0 and negatives. With the current call sites (`order(2)`, `order(3)`) relative ordering still happens to be preserved, but any future use of `order(0)` or a negative value will produce an invalid, ignored legacy declaration, and `order(1)` will be treated as "same as default" in legacy engines while moving the item after default siblings in standard engines. If the legacy prefixes are intended to work, the legacy value should be `$val + 1`; otherwise the legacy declarations should be dropped rather than emitting misleading output.

findings.title: `align-items()` mixin is inconsistent with `flexbox()`: missing `-moz-box-align`, includes a non-existent `-ms-align-items`, and legacy keyword mapping is wrong for flex-start/flex-end
findings.body: `flexbox()` and `order()` emit `-moz-box` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` omits the matching `-moz-box-align`, so any Firefox build that only understands `display: -moz-box` gets the flex layout without the vertical alignment (e.g. header contents would not be centered). The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a property in any IE/Edge release (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11+ uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output on every page. Finally, both `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` use the keywords `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so a future `@include align-items(flex-start)` would silently produce invalid legacy declarations. The current call sites (`center`, `baseline`) are unaffected, but the mixin as written does not deliver the cross-browser fallback it appears to promise.

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make; description is a placeholder
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and the description is just "Test 5". The change replaces float-based layout in the header, small-action posts and category badges with flexbox and adjusts spacing; nothing in it is a performance optimization (flexbox layout is generally no cheaper than floats, and no measurement is provided). The misleading title and empty description will end up in the commit history and make it hard for anyone bisecting a layout regression (e.g. in `.small-action` or the header `.panel`/`.extra-info-wrapper` ordering) to understand the intent. The title and description should describe the actual layout change and its visual effects.
